stories.headline: Google expands Lyria into Lyria 3 Pro with longer tracks and more structure control
stories.summary: Google said Lyria 3 Pro can generate tracks up to three minutes long and better follow prompts for intros, verses, choruses, and bridges. It also embedded music generation into Google Vids, signaling mainstream workflow distribution rather than pure experiment.

stories.headline: IFPI says global recorded music hit $31.7B in 2025 and 837M paid subscriptions
stories.summary: Recorded music remains structurally large and growing even amid AI disruption. Paid subscription streaming grew 8.8% and total streaming revenue surpassed $22B.

stories.headline: UK backs away from favored opt-out AI copyright proposal
stories.summary: The UK government said it no longer favored its earlier opt-out approach for AI training on copyrighted works and now has no preferred option. That is directionally positive for licensing-first models and rightsholder leverage.

stories.headline: Moises/Water & Music survey shows practical AI use is mostly workflow assistance
stories.summary: Among 1,525 surveyed musicians, 78% of professionals said they use AI versus 60% of hobbyists. Stem separation led use cases at 71%, while full-song generation was only 24%, suggesting assistive workflows still dominate real usage.

stories.headline: UNESCO warns music creators could lose 24% of revenue by 2028 from generative AI outputs
stories.summary: UNESCO also highlighted platform concentration and opaque curation systems as ongoing risks for creators. This reinforces the importance of trusted tools and monetization pathways.

stories.headline: TIME reports AI flood and impersonation remain major streaming-layer problems
stories.summary: TIME reported Deezer said 50,000 AI-generated tracks were uploaded daily and made up 34% of new uploads, while Sony had asked platforms to remove 135,000+ tracks impersonating its artists.

stories.headline: Suno's MILO-1080 points toward DAW-adjacent product expansion
stories.summary: Suno is not standing still in pure text-to-song. The MILO-1080 lab experiment suggests continued movement toward sequencer-like creation interfaces and more producer-native workflow positioning.

themes.workflow_over_hype: The strongest evidence still favors AI tools that remove friction in existing music workflows, not tools that fully replace musicians.
themes.rights_cleanliness_matters_more: Policy and public pressure are making clean licensing and rights posture more valuable, not less.
themes.distribution_is_getting_noisier: Spam, impersonation, and AI oversupply are degrading trust at the streaming layer, which increases the value of products associated with quality and control.
themes.musio_implication: Musio should position as trustworthy creator infrastructure: realistic musical output, human control, and commercially usable results rather than mass-volume generative novelty.
